mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units triggers a demand contraction mechanism, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05) or the median return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative equity returns as profit growth expectations deteriorate over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes or the average return is not below the 5th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent surge in real savings (RSAFS) above $500 billion signals a liquidity trap environment, which historically coincides with muted equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% with housing starts (HOUST) above 1.5 million units signals a robust demand expansion, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes or the average return is below the 50th percentile of historical returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes positive equity returns as firms raise prices and invest in capacity over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 100000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods or the median return is below the 50th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for three consecutive months indicates a manufacturing expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes or the average return is below the 50th percentile of historical returns.
